problem: Given that $A=[\begin{aligned}5 & 2\sqrt{5} \\ \sqrt{5} & -3\end{aligned}],$ find the product of the eigenvalues of $A.$

feedback.problem: Given that $A=[\begin{aligned}4 & -8 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}],$ find the sum of the eigenvalues of $A.$
feedback.worked_solution:
The characteristic polynomial of $A$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}p(\lambda ) & ={\lambda }^{2}-\text{tr}(A)\lambda +\text{det}(A).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using Vieta's formulas, we have that the roots of $p(\lambda ),$ i.e. the eigenvalues of $A,$ satisfy

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{1}+{\lambda }_{2}=\text{tr}(A) \\ {\lambda }_{1}\cdot {\lambda }_{2}=\text{det}(A).\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the sum of the eigenvalues of $A$ is equal to the trace of $A.$ 

Therefore, 

$$
{\lambda }_{1}+{\lambda }_{2}=\text{tr}(A)=4+1=5.
$$
